content.value_statement: Large codebases hide repeated structures and unclear architectural choices. This skill finds patterns, explains their intent, and highlights practical refactoring opportunities.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common design patterns using class names, method names, directories, and implementation signatures.
Recognizes architecture styles such as MVC, layered architecture, repository, service layer, and event-driven systems.
Finds repeated code structures, naming conventions, import patterns, and file organization patterns.
Produces pattern reports with locations, purpose, implementation notes, quality assessment, and recommendations.
Includes reference catalogs and a local regex detector for quick pattern signature searches.
limitations: It does not modify code automatically or enforce refactoring decisions.
Regex-based detection can miss subtle patterns or report approximate matches.
Results depend on readable project files and enough context from the target codebase.
Generic reference examples must be validated against the project design and team standards.

use_cases.title: Review a New Codebase
use_cases.description: Identify dominant design and architecture patterns before making changes.

use_cases.title: Plan Refactoring Work
use_cases.description: Find repeated structures, anti-patterns, and extraction opportunities with file references.

use_cases.title: Improve Code Reviews
use_cases.description: Check whether pattern usage is consistent, appropriate, and easy to maintain.

prompt_templates.title: Find Design Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this codebase for design patterns. List each pattern, location, purpose, quality, and recommended next step.

prompt_templates.title: Check Repeated Structures
prompt_templates.prompt: Find repeated code structures in this project. Group them by similarity and suggest practical refactoring options.

prompt_templates.title: Map Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the application architecture. Identify layers, data flow, boundaries, strengths, weaknesses, and pattern consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Pattern Refactors
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare pattern issues by impact and effort. Recommend a prioritized refactoring plan with risks and expected benefits.

output_examples.input: What design patterns are used in this codebase?
output_examples.output: The report identifies factory, observer, repository, and service layer patterns with locations, intent, quality notes, and follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Find repeated code in the project.
output_examples.output: The output groups similar validation, data fetching, and error handling structures, then recommends shared utilities or hooks where useful.
The summary describes the main architecture style, layer responsibilities, data flow, strengths, boundary gaps, and improvement priorities.

best_practices: Ask for pattern findings with file references and impact, not only pattern names.
Validate each detected pattern against the real code before planning refactors.
Use the recommendations to improve maintainability, not to force unnecessary patterns.
anti_patterns: Treating every repeated structure as a problem without checking context.
Applying design patterns only because they are familiar or popular.
Ignoring architecture boundaries when proposing local code cleanup.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes code organization, design patterns, architecture patterns, naming conventions, repeated structures, and anti-patterns.

faq.question: Does it change my code?
faq.answer: No. It reports findings and recommendations, but it does not edit files by itself.

faq.question: Can it detect duplicate code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify repeated structures and likely duplication, then suggest extraction or consolidation options.

faq.question: Does it require a specific language?
faq.answer: No. The guidance is general, and the included detector focuses on common TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, Go, and Rust files.

faq.question: How reliable are the findings?
faq.answer: The findings are best treated as analysis leads. Human review should confirm intent, quality, and refactoring value.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
